stories.title: Clarion Partners Acquires Grocery-Anchored Fairfield County Retail
stories.excerpt: Franklin Templeton and its real estate investment manager Clarion Partners announced Clarion Partners Real Estate Income Fund Inc.’s acquisition of Main Avenue Shopping Plaza, a 156,568-square-foot grocery-anchored community shopping center in Norwalk, CT. The purchase price was not disclosed. JLL represented the seller, a joint venture between Sagehall Partners and The Prusik Group. Located in densely populated Fairfield County, Main Avenue Shopping Plaza is fully leased to a roster of nationally recognized retailers led by Stop & Shop, Hobby Lobby, and Total Wine & More. The 16-acre property has served the local community for nearly three decades and benefits from a prominent location at the intersection of Main Avenue, U.S. Route 7, and the Merritt Parkway “This acquisition reflects continued conviction in well-located, grocery-anchored retail centers that provide durable cash flow and potential long-term value creation,” said Clarion Transactions VP Taylor Epperson. “Main Avenue Shopping Plaza combines exceptional real estate fundamentals with a highly stable tenant roster serving an affluent and growing consumer base. The property’s strong occupancy, long-term leases and strategic location make it an excellent opportunity for our investors.” The post Clarion Partners Acquires Grocery-Anchored Fairfield County Retail appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Clarion Partners acquires 156k SF grocery-anchored center in Norwalk, CT for undisclosed price.
Stop & Shop, Hobby Lobby, Total Wine anchor fully leased 16-acre property.
Dense Fairfield County location signals investor conviction in stable retail cash flows.
stories.summary: Franklin Templeton's Clarion Partners acquired Main Avenue Shopping Plaza, a fully leased 156,568-square-foot grocery-anchored community center in Norwalk, CT, anchored by Stop & Shop, Hobby Lobby, and Total Wine & More. The 16-acre property is 100% leased with a strong tenant roster serving an affluent Fairfield County demographic. Clarion cited durable cash flow and long-term lease stability as investment drivers.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact. Retail acquisitions in affluent suburbs reflect capital pursuit of stable yields, but do not signal demand tailwinds or land availability for apartment development in Fairfield County.

stories.title: Bill Ackman Buys 125 West End Avenue for $260M Brain Research Institute
stories.excerpt: Billionaire hedge funder Bill Ackman has kicked off his $260 million play to establish a brain research institute on Manhattan’s Upper West Side. Pershing Square Foundation, the philanthropic arm of Ackman’s fund, dropped $188 million to acquire 125 West End Avenue, according to city documents filed Tuesday. The 400,000-square-foot life sciences building planned for the site will eventually host Ackman’s massive brain research center, the Ackman Oxman Institute, Fortune first reported. The sale by Taconic Partners reportedly precedes another in-contract sale for the neighboring building, 320 West 66th Street, for roughly $70 million. Together, the acquisitions would secure Pershing Square Foundation an estimated 700,000 square feet of research and office space between West 65th and West 66th streets. Ackman told Fortune that the charitable venture was inspired by his 26-year-old daughter, Lucy, who previously suffered a brain hemorrhage, as well as his wife, Neri Oxman, who lost her mother to Alzheimer’s disease. Pershing Square Foundation has teamed up with Mount Sinai Hospital System to develop the research institute, although the development timeline is unclear. The life sciences and office spaces at 125 West End Avenue, also called West End Labs, appear largely vacant, according to the building’s website. The building belongs to a 3.4-acre campus, known as West End Campus, sold to Taconic by Silverstein Properties for $230 million in 2019. West End Campus also includes 320 West 66th Street and a vacant parcel. Taconic repositioned the campus as a purpose-built research and laboratory complex. Its previous lives include the American Broadcasting Company (ABC)’s former campus, a Chrysler Motor Company facility and printing facilities for The New York Times. Spokespeople for Pershing Square Foundation and Taconic did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Foundation acquires 125 West End Ave for $188M on Manhattan's Upper West Side.
400k SF life sciences building planned; combined 700k SF acquisition with neighboring 320 West 66th Street (~$70M).
Conversion of office/mixed-use to life sciences and research campus removes rental residential land from market.
stories.summary: Billionaire Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Foundation spent $188 million to acquire 125 West End Avenue on Manhattan's Upper West Side, with plans for a 400,000-square-foot life sciences building. A second in-contract acquisition at 320 West 66th Street (~$70 million) will secure an estimated 700,000 square feet of research and office space for the Ackman Oxman Institute brain research center. The philanthropic venture was inspired by Ackman's family health challenges.
stories.impact: Upper West Side Manhattan: Large-scale conversion of ~700k SF mixed-use/office footprint to life sciences and research removes potential adaptive-reuse residential supply and signals capital flight from office to specialized research uses. Tightens available trophy real estate for multifamily redevelopment in one of Manhattan's strongest demographic corridors.

stories.title: Goulston & Storrs Adds Brian Grindall to Real Estate Practice
stories.excerpt: Brian Grindall, a veteran commercial real estate attorney who spent nearly 16 years at Tenenbaum & Saas in Washington, D.C., has joined law firm Goulston & Storrs, Commercial Observer has learned. Grindall has been added to Goulston & Storrs’ real estate group as a director in the firm’s Washington, D.C., office. In addition to his time at Tenenbaum & Saas where he ascended to partner, Grindall was previously a general counsel at development firm the Opus Group, according to his Linkedin profile. “Brian has built an impressive practice advising clients on their most significant transactions,” Paul Tummonds Jr., director and administrative head of Goulston & Storrs’ D.C. office, said in a statement. “His experience, practical business perspective, and ability to navigate complex real estate matters make him an outstanding addition to our firm.” In his more than two-decade legal career, Grindall has advised CRE parties on a variety of deals including acquisitions, dispositions, financing, leasing and development. His practice also involves advising on joint ventures, loan workouts and restructuring of distressed properties. Grindall earned his master’s in real estate from Johns Hopkins University, his law degree from New England Law and his B.A. from the College of Wooster. “Goulston & Storrs has built an outstanding real estate platform and a reputation for delivering practical, business-focused counsel,” Grindall said in a statement. “I was drawn to the firm’s collaborative culture and the opportunity to work alongside a team that shares my commitment to helping clients solve complex real estate challenges.” Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Goulston & Storrs hires Brian Grindall, 16-year veteran from Tenenbaum & Saas, as real estate director.
Grindall was general counsel at Opus Group, advises on acquisitions, financing, development, and joint ventures.
Lawyer hiring reflects no material market signal; administrative/staffing news only.
stories.summary: Law firm Goulston & Storrs hired Brian Grindall, a 16-year partner at Tenenbaum & Saas and former general counsel at Opus Group, as a director in its Washington, D.C. real estate practice. Grindall has advised on acquisitions, dispositions, financing, leasing, development, and joint ventures across two decades.
stories.impact: No material impact on multifamily supply, demand, capital, or cost. This is personnel/firm expansion news and does not signal market conditions.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation Arranges $16M for Green Bay MF Construction
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation (MMCC) arranged $16.54 million in financing for the construction of Common Place Phase II, a 91-unit mixed-use multifamily property with a first-floor retail unit located within walking distance to Lambeau Stadium at 670 Mike McCarthy Way in Green Bay, Wisconsin.Robert Bhat, senior managing director in MMCC’s Miami office, secured the financing at 80% loan-to-cost with a local bank on behalf of the client. The loan features a five-year term, with a 6.25% interest rate and no prepayment penalty. The residential unit mix includes studios, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom units designed to complement the adjacent Phase I development and capture continued rental demand in the submarket. The Common Place is a five-story mixed-use building on a former industrial site in the Village of Ashwaubenon’s Sports & Entertainment District. Construction commenced in June on the development. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. The post Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation Arranges $16M for Green Bay MF Construction appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap arranges $16.54M construction financing for 91-unit mixed-use at 670 Mike McCarthy Way, Green Bay.
80% LTC, 6.25% rate, 5-year term, no prepay penalty; located near Lambeau Stadium in Sports & Entertainment District.
Phase II captures rental demand from adjacent Phase I; conversion of former industrial site in recovering submarket.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation arranged $16.54 million in construction financing for Common Place Phase II, a 91-unit mixed-use multifamily property with ground-floor retail in Green Bay, Wisconsin, near Lambeau Stadium. The loan closed at 80% loan-to-cost with a local bank at 6.25% for five years with no prepayment penalty. Construction commenced in June on the five-story development in the Sports & Entertainment District.
stories.impact: Green Bay submarket: Stadium-proximate multifamily development with captured demand from Phase I signals landlord conviction in event-driven rental absorption near Lambeau. 6.25% construction rate indicates regional lender availability and modest cost pressure; development feasibility remains strong in secondary markets with anchor tenants.

stories.title: VP Eric Jeremiah Joins CBRE’s Greater Boston Office Leasing Team
stories.excerpt: Eric Jeremiah has joined CBRE as a VP in the organization’s Greater Boston suburban office brokerage business. Jeremiah will focus on both tenant and landlord representation. “We are pleased to welcome Eric to our suburban office practice in Greater Boston,” said Mike Brucato, executive managing director and Greater Boston market leader at CBRE. “He is a highly respected office broker with deep market knowledge and a strong track record of success advising both landlords and occupiers.” Before joining CBRE, Jeremiah spent over five years with Newmark, where he represented tenants and landlords on suburban office and industrial leasing assignments throughout Greater Boston. He graduated from Middlebury College, where he was a member of the varsity lacrosse team. The post VP Eric Jeremiah Joins CBRE’s Greater Boston Office Leasing Team appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE hires Eric Jeremiah as VP in Greater Boston suburban office brokerage.
Jeremiah moves from Newmark after 5+ years; focuses on tenant and landlord representation.
Broker hiring reflects no material market signal; staffing/competitive repositioning only.
stories.summary: Eric Jeremiah joined CBRE as a VP in its Greater Boston suburban office brokerage business, transitioning from a 5+ year tenure at Newmark. He will focus on tenant and landlord representation in suburban office and industrial leasing.
stories.impact: No material impact on multifamily supply, demand, capital, or cost. This is talent movement between brokerages and does not indicate market conditions.

stories.title: Sares Regis Trades South San Francisco Multifamily to Bell Partners
stories.excerpt: Sares Regis Group of Northern California and Bell Partners LLC announced the sale of Celeste Apartments, a 195-unit multifamily community in South San Francisco. The LEED Silver certified property, located at 401 Cypress Ave. and adjacent to the Caltrain station, was acquired by Bell Partners on behalf of its Bell Growth & Income Fund investors and will be renamed Bell South City II. The seller, a partnership between Sares Regis and an institutional equity partner, was represented by Berkadia in San Francisco. The acquisition price was undisclosed. Celeste Apartments is the second Sares Regis property acquired by Bell Partners, following the $206-million sale of nearby Cadence in 2022. “Sares Regis has been a pioneer in multifamily residential development in South San Francisco, bringing 455 apartments to market, starting with Cadence in 2019 and its neighbor Celeste welcoming residents three years later,” said Drew Hudacek, CIO for Sares Regis. “We are proud to have helped advance the city’s vision for its downtown under the Downtown Station Area Specific Plan.” The post Sares Regis Trades South San Francisco Multifamily to Bell Partners appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sares Regis sells 195-unit Celeste Apartments in South San Francisco to Bell Partners for undisclosed price.
LEED Silver property at 401 Cypress Ave adjacent to Caltrain station; rebranded Bell South City II.
Second Sares Regis property sale to Bell Partners; signals institutional capital consolidation near transit in high-cost submarket.
stories.summary: Sares Regis Group sold Celeste Apartments, a 195-unit LEED Silver-certified multifamily community in South San Francisco, to Bell Partners, which acquired it on behalf of its Bell Growth & Income Fund. The property at 401 Cypress Avenue is adjacent to the Caltrain station and will be renamed Bell South City II. This is Bell Partners' second South San Francisco acquisition from Sares Regis, following the 2022 purchase of Cadence for $206 million.
stories.impact: South San Francisco/Silicon Valley Peninsula: Repeat institutional acquisitions of Sares Regis' transit-proximate, recently delivered multifamily signify strong cap-rate arbitrage and core-plus yields in Bay Area markets despite regulatory/cost headwinds. Consolidation of pipeline product into growth funds indicates investor confidence in Peninsula rental demand and limited new supply competition near Caltrain.

stories.title: Phoenix Leads Nation in Hotel Openings
stories.excerpt: The Phoenix metro will have more hotels open this year than any other major city in the United States. The Valley of the Sun is expected to have 26 hotel projects open before the end of the year. The Phoenix Business Journal reports that accounts for 3,615 new hotel rooms being added to the regional market, per Lodging Econometrics’ Q2 2026 United States Construction Pipeline Trend Report. Phoenix beat out New York and Dallas, with both of those cities forecasted to have 20 new projects, followed by California’s Inland Empire with 12 and Austin, Texas, with 11 new hotel openings in 2026. In downtown Mesa, Hospitality Capital Partners opened 233 Suites Unscripted by Hyatt within the Grid mixed-use development that features 76 suite-style guest rooms with full kitchens. In the spring, the AC Hotel Scottsdale Old Town opened, adding 168 rooms in the Valley’s upscale-hotel room inventory. In mid-September, the 236-room Denū Hotel & Spa (shown) will open at 1 E Adams St. The post Phoenix Leads Nation in Hotel Openings appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Phoenix metro leads U.S. with 26 hotel openings planned in 2026, adding 3,615 new rooms.
Beats New York and Dallas (20 projects each); Inland Empire (12), Austin (11) follow.
Hotel supply boom in Phoenix reflects tourism and convention demand but does not directly signal multifamily rental growth.
stories.summary: The Phoenix metro is forecasted to have 26 hotel projects open in 2026, the most of any major U.S. city, adding 3,615 new rooms. Phoenix leads New York and Dallas (20 projects each), followed by the Inland Empire (12) and Austin (11). Recent openings include Suites Unscripted by Hyatt in downtown Mesa (233 rooms), AC Hotel Scottsdale Old Town (168 rooms), and the Denū Hotel & Spa (236 rooms).
stories.impact: Phoenix metro: Heavy hospitality supply pipeline signals strong tourism/convention demand and capital allocation to leisure/travel, but does not directly correlate to multifamily rental demand unless tied to corporate relocation or population in-migration. Monitor whether hotel expansion attracts service/support jobs and housing demand in suburban Phoenix markets.

stories.title: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Takes 5K SF at 1733 Eastchester Road in the Bronx
stories.excerpt: Simone Development Companies has brought its two-story, 27,275-square-foot medical and office building at 1733 Eastchester Road in the Bronx’s Morris Park neighborhood to full occupancy, according to the firm. The building’s last vacant space was leased in June, when the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) inked a long-term, 5,234-square-foot lease to house the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs’ new Bronx Vet Center at the property. It was a direct lease between the GSA and Simone. The Bronx vet center will provide counseling, outreach and referral services to veterans and service members, as well as their families. The Department of Veterans Affairs has several other vet centers in New York City, including locations in Ridgewood, Queens, Downtown Brooklyn and in Midtown. The asking rent in the deal was not disclosed, but the average asking rent for office space in the Bronx was $39.46 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to research by PropertyShark. The vet center’s lease brought Simone’s 1733 Eastchester Road to full occupancy after the landlord also signed a 2,766-square-foot lease in May with Downtown Brooklyn Physical Therapy to open the medical service provider’s first Bronx location. The length of that lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. Simone was also represented in-house in this deal, while the tenant was represented by Gary Mayzlin from Real Estate Trade Company. Mayzlin did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “The full lease-up of 1733 Eastchester Road reflects the growing need for well-located and high-quality outpatient medical and social services space in the Bronx,” Joe Simone, president of Simone, said in a statement. “We’re thrilled that the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and Downtown Brooklyn PT chose this property, which offers great visibility, modern professional space, and a strategic location to accommodate the expanding needs of these vital service providers.” Other tenants at 17
bullets: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs leases 5,234 SF at 1733 Eastchester Road, Bronx via GSA.
Simone Development achieves 100% occupancy at 27,275 SF medical/office building in Morris Park.
Federal tenant (Bronx Vet Center) provides stable, long-term income; no multifamily signal.
stories.summary: Simone Development Companies leased its final 5,234 square feet at 1733 Eastchester Road in the Bronx's Morris Park neighborhood to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (via GSA) for a new Vet Center providing counseling, outreach, and referral services. The two-story, 27,275-square-foot medical and office building achieved 100% occupancy. Average asking rent for office space in the Bronx was $39.46/SF in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Bronx/Morris Park: Federal occupancy of medical office building signals modest institutional demand but does not generate multifamily rental demand. Office building stabilization in secondary Bronx submarket indicates slow but stable commercial recovery; no direct supply or demand catalyst for apartments.

stories.title: Whole Foods Signs 8K-SF Lease to Open Daily Shop at 1524 Second Avenue
stories.excerpt: Whole Foods Market has signed a lease to open its version of a mini-mart on the Upper East Side. The Amazon-owned grocery chain closed an 8,121-square-foot deal for one of its small-scale concepts on the ground floor of ConTowers Associates LP’s 1524 Second Avenue, also known as the Continental Towers, according to landlord broker Newmark. While the brokers did not define what kind of concept the store will be, the focus will be on prepared foods in a convenient setting. It will likely be part of the grocer’s Whole Foods Market Daily Shop concept, which launched in March 2024. Newmark did not disclose the asking rent length of the lease but said the asking rent was $250 per square foot. “This transaction presented a unique opportunity to secure a highly visible corner location in one of Manhattan’s most established neighborhood retail corridors,” Newmark’s Jeffrey Roseman, who represented the landlord alongside Drew Weiss, said in a statement. “The combination of the property’s location, visibility and surrounding residential density made it an excellent fit for Whole Foods Market’s neighborhood store format.” Chase Welles and Jacqueline Klinger of The Shopping Center Group negotiated on behalf of Whole Foods, but did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Whole Foods has been expanding its daily shop presence in New York City lately, signing a ​​15-year, 10,000-square-foot lease at 1224 Flushing Avenue in Bushwick, Brooklyn, in June for the bodega-branded concept. In January, however, the e-commerce giant announced it would close all of its Amazon Go and Amazon Fresh locations in an effort to focus on Whole Foods as a brand and on its online grocery delivery services. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Whole Foods Market signs 8,121 SF lease at 1524 Second Avenue (Continental Towers), Upper East Side Manhattan.
Amazon-owned grocer opens Daily Shop concept (prepared foods focus); asking rent $250/SF.
Grocery retail anchoring premium Manhattan ground floor; signals continued retail demand in trophy neighborhoods.
stories.summary: Whole Foods Market signed an 8,121-square-foot lease on the ground floor of 1524 Second Avenue (Continental Towers) on Manhattan's Upper East Side to open a Daily Shop concept focused on prepared foods. The asking rent was $250 per square foot. Whole Foods launched its Daily Shop small-format concept in March 2024.
stories.impact: Upper East Side Manhattan: Amazon-backed Whole Foods deployment to premium Manhattan retail signals retail capital confidence in established affluent neighborhoods and high rent absorption. Grocery retail anchoring strengthens adjacent residential appeal and supports multifamily rental demand in the corridor, but does not directly expand supply.

stories.title: Northwest Bank Lends $28M on East Hartford Industrial Buy
stories.excerpt: Seyon Group has sealed $28.1 million of acquisition financing to purchase an 11-building industrial campus in East Hartford, Conn., Commercial Observer has learned. Northwest Bank supplied the loan for Seyon Group’s $37 million acquisition of the 428,000-square-foot Prestige Park property. The 11 warehouses that comprise the industrial campus were previously owned by investors tied to entities Barrington TIC, Market Street TIC II, ACG Prestige Acquisitions and JR Prestige Spe, according to East Hartford town documents. Newmark negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Chris Kramer, Timothy O’Donnell, Max Ralby, Conor Reenstierna and Amel Vernon. Brian Schulz, managing director at Newmark, arranged the sale representing the seller, which was not disclosed by the brokerage firm. Situated on nearly 29 acres six miles east of Downtown Hartford, Prestige Park features a mix of single-tenant, mid-bay and shallow-bay industrial buildings. The industrial campus is around 94 percent leased to manufacturing, research and development, warehouse and distribution tenants, according to Newmark. It also includes two developable land parcels for future expansion options. Northwest Bank and Seyon Group did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Seyon Group acquires 428k SF industrial campus (11 buildings) in East Hartford, CT for $37M with $28.1M debt.
Northwest Bank finances; Prestige Park on 29 acres is 94% leased to manufacturing, R&D, warehouse tenants.
Industrial acquisition signals regional lender availability and manufacturing demand but no multifamily nexus.
stories.summary: Seyon Group acquired the 11-building Prestige Park industrial campus in East Hartford, Connecticut, for $37 million with $28.1 million of acquisition financing from Northwest Bank. The 428,000-square-foot complex on 29 acres comprises single-tenant, mid-bay, and shallow-bay industrial buildings and is 94% leased to manufacturing, research and development, and warehouse tenants. The property is situated six miles east of downtown Hartford.
stories.impact: East Hartford/Hartford region: Industrial acquisition and lease momentum signal manufacturing and R&D job retention/growth in Connecticut, which could support incremental multifamily demand in Hartford and nearby submarkets if employment grows. However, no direct supply or zoning signals; monitor whether manufacturing/R&D payroll expansion translates to worker housing demand in affordable outer-ring Hartford suburbs.
